messages:
support_jordan: Heads-up — AcmeCorp just escalated: their webhook POSTs from our private VPC started getting 403s around 11:05 UTC. They say nothing changed on their side. They were using an allowlist of our SNAT IPs. Can infra confirm recent SNAT churn?

net-lee: I saw a NAT pool rebalance earlier during an autoscale event. Investigating mapping now.

infra-bot: alert: snat-rebalance completed 1902345600; old_pool: 10.144.5.0/28 -> old_ips [34.77.125.10, 34.77.125.11]; new_pool: 10.144.9.0/28 -> new_ips [35.212.214.9, 35.212.214.10] (sticky-session=false)

maya: ":thinking_face:" customer firewall likely still has old IPs. Did the rebalance require sticky SNAT?

net-lee: It was a normal rebalance to spread connections after scale. We didn't enable sticky SNAT for that node group. That explains allowlist drift.

support_jordan: Can we either (A) restore previous SNAT IPs for that customer's VPC or (B) notify the customer to add the new IPs? They asked for a fast workaround.

sre-rita: Short-term: we can add a transient mapping to preserve previous egress for AcmeCorp's subnet. I'll trigger a sticky SNAT mapping for their VPC for 2 hours while they update allowlists.

net-lee: FYI the flow to add transient mapping: `gcloud compute routers nats update <nat-name> --nat-external-ip-pool <ip-range>` (internal runbook link: https://confluence/redwood/nat-runbook). Will do once support opens a change ticket.

support_jordan: I'll open a change and ping the customer with the new IPs once it's live. Also requested they flush firewall DNS caches — some customers use DNS to map hostnames to our egress IPs (which can be cached stale).

maya: Suggest we also recommend customers use our stable egress hostname (egress.redwood-inference.net) that points to a managed set with SLA and low churn, rather than raw IPs.

sre-rita: Agreed. For the immediate case, I'm applying sticky mapping now. Will post confirmation and the 2 new IPs to share.

infra-bot: action: sticky-snat apply start 1902345745 -> target_vpc acme-prod-vpc, duration 7200s. allocated_ips [34.77.125.10, 34.77.125.11]

support_jordan: Customer updated. They see 200s for the last 3 tests after applying fixes. Leaving them an ask: add both old and new IPs to allowlist for 72h.

net-lee: Follow-ups: (1) add monitoring alert if SNAT change affects >1 customer in same tenant, (2) evaluate enabling sticky by default for private VPCs with webhook-heavy customers, (3) update docs/runbook to include recommended allowlist TTL guidance (min 48h).

sre-rita: I'll create GH issue for runbook + sticky-by-default proposal.

support_jordan: Customer happy for now, closing the immediate loop. Recording request: require a proactive customer notification after scheduled maintenance that may touch NAT pools. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy status: no ongoing deployments in the private-vpc region at time of incident.
